text:
Commissions & Boards

1.
Overview
The Department of City Planning facilitates a number of boards, commissions, panels, and development activities meetings (DAMs) which review zoning variances and elements of development, design, public art, and historic preservation.

For additional information on a board, commission, or panel, such as appointed members or past meeting minutes, navigate to the table of contents or through the sections at the bottom of this page.

2.
Contextual Design Advisory Panel

CDAP meets every other Tuesday, alternating with Planning Commission

The Contextual Design Advisory Panel (CDAP) is comprised of eight members with expertise in the physical development of the City. The panel's mission is to promote quality of life in the City of Pittsburgh. CDAP achieves its mission through professional, voluntary design assistance to maximize the economic, civic, contextual, and aesthetic value of new development projects impacting the public realm. To fulfill this mission, CDAP advises the Department of City Planning by reviewing and providing design guidance on selected, higher profile projects throughout the City.

CDAP is an advisory panel, not a commission. Together with staff design review, the panel works to resolve design issues through professional peer critique before a Commission conducts its review. This frees the the Commission to focus on its responsibility of assuring that new developments are consistent with the overall planning objectives of the City. Some examples of these core considerations are:

The extent to which each development proposal addresses successful design, public space enhancement, context sensitivity and sustainable urbanism.

Ensuring that projects feature well designed buildings and landscapes that engage both users and the streetscape. Buildings should also make appropriate connections to adjacent sites and to the larger neighborhood.

The use of sustainable building materials and designs which consider the longer-term impact and use of a single project.

CDAP Members

Contextual Design Advisory Panel Members

Eric Booth, AIA

Bruce Chan

Sara Harris, AIA

Ryan Indovina, RA, LEED AP

Greg LaForest, AIA, LEED AP

Cassandra Osterman, AIA

Peter Quintanilla

Bob Reppe

Claudia Saladin, ASLA, LEED AP

CDAP Meeting Material

Presentations are required to be submitted by EOD the Tuesday before the scheduled meeting date. Presentations should include:

Items that address Staff Design Review comments and Urban Design Targets

Site plan showing proposed project and surrounding context

Landscape plan showing surrounding context and proposed planting list

Building elevations showing surrounding context and proposed materials

Building sections showing site context

Perspective views and renderings showing project in surrounding context

Perspective views and renderings showing pedestrian context and sidewalk-level views

Meeting Format and Review

CDAP meetings are held virtually every other Tuesday from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM and 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM The typical meeting format follows:

Brief project introduction by staff (5 minutes)

Project presentation by Applicant (15 minutes)

Panel discussion (40 minutes)

As CDAP is not a Commission, the Panel does not vote on projects. After each review, City Planning staff provides a summary of comments to the applicant and if applicable, to the necessary Board or Commission.

On certain occasions, a second review may be recommended by staff. The purpose of a second meeting is to resolve outstanding urban design goals. In addition to standard CDAP reviews, a workshop format may also be used for projects in an early stage of development. Less like a formal review, a workshop is more of collaborative meeting to provide design guidance to applicants.

In rare instances, CDAP members may be asked to review a project over email when a full meeting is not necessary.

To contact CDAP via email, please email pacd@pittsburghpa.gov

CDAP Process Guide
(PDF, 106KB)

3.
Historic Review Commission

The Historic Review Commission meets on the first Wednesday of each month. Meetings starts at 1:00 PM.

The Historic Review Commission (HRC) provides guidance to those seeking to conduct exterior work on historic buildings in the city. The Historic Review Commission is comprised of seven members appointed by the Mayor. The membership of the commission must include a professional preservationist or an active architectural historian, an architect, a representative from the Department of City Planning, a representative from the Department of Permits, Licenses, and Inspections, a Real Estate sales community representative, and two community residents who have demonstrated an outstanding interest and / or knowledge of historic preservation and restoration in the City of Pittsburgh.

The Historic Review Commission has control over any proposed new construction or demolition within a historic district and exterior work to a historic landmark. The review process begins when an owner decides to work to the building. To start an application, visit City Planning's Historic Preservation page.

4.
Naming Commission

The Naming Commission meets quarterly and is held virtually.

The Commission on Naming Public Properties creates guidelines and specifications for naming or changing the name of public property or facilities. These guidelines and specifications include:

How to receive requests and recommendations

Provisions for public hearings and meetings

A facility or public property can only be named or renamed for a person after that person has been deceased for at least three years

Naming or renaming a public property or facility for an individual person can only be recommended and approved if that person has been deceased for at least three years

Director of Department of Public Works ; Member

The Naming Commission completes a report on the property or facility being named or renamed. This report includes the historic, artistic, and cultural background of any facility proposed to be named or renamed. For more information about the Naming Commission, please email City Planning at cityplanning@pittsburghpa.gov.

5.
Planning Commission

Planning Commission meets every other Tuesday, with an August recess. Meetings start at 1:00 PM.

The Planning Commission is a nine-member panel appointed by the Mayor for six-year, staggered terms. The Commission is charged with guiding land use and land development within the City. The Planning Commission also makes recommendations to City Council concerning the Zoning Ordinance and zoning maps, and reviews major development, redevelopment proposals, master plans, conditional uses, lot consolidations and subdivisions, and historic nominations.

6.
Public Art & Civic Design Commission

The PACD Commission meets on the fourth Wednesday of each month, with a December recess. Meetings start at 2:00 PM

The City of Pittsburgh’s Public Art & Civic Design Commission empowers the development of art and culture in public spaces and promotes the design of public spaces and civic structures that have a positive impact on the City’s Public Realm. For that purpose, the Commission is authorized to review and approve the aesthetics of the designed environment on or over City-owned property.

The Commission conducts reviews through two Committees:

The
Public Art Review Committee
reviews and approves the addition, modification, relocation, and removal of items of Public Art in the Public Realm.

The
Civic Design Review Committee
reviews and approves the design of new structures and designed sites in the Public Realm, or the modification of existing structures and designed sites in the Public Realm.

To receive Commissions and Board agendas via email, please email pacd@pittsburghpa.gov

Over-the-Counter Review

Over-The-Counter (OTC) review is conducted by City Planning staff for low-impact projects that meet certain eligibility criteria. Reviews are limited to proposed projects that will have a relatively minimal impact on the public realm. Projects may be eligible for Over-The-Counter approval based on the following criteria:

Replacements: Projects which replace the form or content of existing elements or fixtures in order to repair, improve, or update existing implementations. Replacements may be either of the following:

In Kind: Repair or replacement of existing elements or fixtures with identical products, or products of a similar aesthetic that have been slightly modified due to changes in cost, product availability, or updates.

Content: Changes made to written content or images in order to provide updated information, branding, or imagery which maintain the same overall aesthetic.

Negligible Changes: Projects that will have minimal to no impact on the public realm. Negligible changes may be either of the following:

Low Visibility: Changes or additions that cannot be easily viewed from public property or the right-of-way.

Minor change: Changes or additions that will not affect the general aesthetic of the site, would go unnoticed by a large portion of visitors to the site, or would be assumed by most viewers to be a standard element of City infrastructure.

City Standards: Projects that fit within the City’s established design standards.

Modifications: Changes to the design and/or aesthetic of projects that have previously been approved by the Public Art & Civic Design Commission.

To learn more about Over-the-Counter Review, please download the PACD Commission Manual. Applications for OTC Review are submitted through the PACD Commission Application form.

7.
Zoning Board of Adjustment

The ZBA meets on the first three Thursdays of each month. Meetings start at 9:00 AM

The Zoning Board of Adjustment (ZBA) is an adjudicative body that reviews land use proposals in accordance with the requirements of the Zoning Code. The Board reviews such matters in public evidentiary hearings at which the applicant and impacted neighbors may submit evidence or testimony in support of or in opposition to the request.

Zoning Board of Adjustment Members

Lashawn Burton-Falk

Alice Mitinger

John J. Richardson

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

How long does it take for the ZBA to issue a decision?

The ZBA is part of the Zoning Review process. The Zoning Code requires a minimum 21-day posted notice period before a ZBA hearing. Following a hearing, the ZBA has 45 days to issue a decision.

Link to Zoning Review process:

How is a ZBA hearing scheduled?

Applicants to the ZBA are required to file a Zoning and Development Review (ZDR) Application, which is submitted online through the OneStopPGH portal. After the Department of City Planning has reviewed a ZDR application and determined that it requires a ZBA hearing, it will contact the Applicant to schedule a hearing date. For assistance with filing a ZDR application, contact zoning@pittsburghpa.gov. The $400 ZBA fee is assessed in addition to the base zoning review fees. Reference the Fee Schedule for information about other review fees. Fees are non-refundable, regardless of whether a request to the ZBA is approved or denied. Payment must be made prior to the hearing. Fees can be paid via credit card or E-check through the OneStopPGH portal.

What is the public notification process?

ZBA agendas are posted online on City Planning's Public Meetings Calendar and sent via email. To receive agendas via email, please zoningboard@pittsburghpa.gov

How will neighbors be notified?

The Department of City Planning mails notice letters to abutting property owners. The ZBA also strongly recommended that Applicants contact neighbors and local community organizations in advance of a hearing. The Department of City Planning can provide contact information for relevant community groups. If a project is in an area with a Registered Community Organization (RCO), a Development Activities Meeting with the RCO may be required at least 30 days before the ZBA hearing.

What materials are needed at the Hearing?

Applicants must provide:

A site plan which details the proposal

Evidence which justifies the approval of the request, in accordance with the Zoning Code’s approval criteria

Applicants who are not the owner of the property must be prepared to explain and document their authorization to pursue the request

The Applicant must provide sufficient evidence to justify the approval of the request. All parties, Applicants and interested parties can present evidence to the Board. Helpful evidence may include:

Photographs of the property and the surrounding neighborhood

Elevations and detailed drawings of the proposal

Business or operational plans

Evidence that demonstrates how the proposal will affect the surrounding neighborhood

Evidence that demonstrates how the proposal does or does not meet the Zoning Code’s approval criteria

When will the ZBA decision be issued?

After the record for a hearing is closed, the ZBA will issue a decision within 45 days. This decision is sent to the Applicant and all parties who testified at the hearing. Usually, the ZBA will close the record at the end of a hearing. Occasionally, for complex cases, or projects with considerable community opposition, the ZBA will keep the record open after a hearing to allow submittal of additional evidence.

What happens after a decision is issued?

After the ZBA has issued a decision, the Department of City Planning will continue to review the application for compliance with Zoning Code. When the Department of City Planning determines that an application complies with the Zoning Code, it will issue a Record of Zoning Approval (ROZA). Once an applicant receives a ROZA, they may need to apply for additional permits from the Department of Permits, Licenses, and Inspections.

Do ZBA decisions expire?

A ZBA decision expires one year after it is issued. A permit should be obtained and substantial construction or occupancy should begin within one year of approval. If additional time is needed, An Applicant may request a one-year extension by contacting zoningboard@pittsburghpa.gov, and providing a brief explanation of why an extension is needed.

May the ZBA decision be appealed?

Any affected party may appeal a ZBA decision to the Court of Common Pleas of Allegheny County within 30 calendar days of the decision’s issue date. The appeal process starts at the Department of Court Records located on the main floor of the City-County Building, 414 Grant Street. A transcript of the ZBA hearing will be required. Appellants are strongly encouraged to consult an attorney.

Where can transcripts be requested?

You can order a transcript of a ZBA hearing by calling Network Deposition Services at 412-281-7908. Network Deposition Services will charge a fee to access the transcript. Please have the case number and hearing date available.

Are ZBA agendas available?

ZBA agendas are posted online on City Planning's Public Meetings Calendar and sent via email. To receive agendas via email, please zoningboard@pittsburghpa.gov

Are ZBA meetings public?

ZBA meetings are open to the public are held virtually via Zoom or in-person in the Lower Level Hearing Room at 412 Boulevard of the Allies. Community members impacted by requests to the ZBA are encouraged to attend and present testimony. Visit City Planning's Public Meetings Calendar for more information on meeting agenda, times, and Zoom meeting links.

Are past ZBA decisions publicly available?

To request a copy of a ZBA decision, contact zoningboard@pittsburghpa.gov

For previous year's meeting presentations, please visit City Planning's YouTube page. You may also order a transcript of a meeting by calling Network Deposition Services at 412-281-7908. text:
Trick-or-Treat Hours for City of Pittsburgh

Next date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 | 05:30 PM
to 07:30 PM

“Pittsburghers love to celebrate Halloween and all of the fun annual community traditions for our kids, families and neighbors,” said Mayor O’Connor. “I want to thank the community organizations who host events and our whole City and CitiParks team for being creative and coming up with fun new ways to bring our neighborhoods together. Let’s all do our part to make sure our kids have a safe and fun Halloween.”

The City recommends the following safety tips for trick-or-treaters:

Include reflective tape, stickers or clip-on lights on costumes and bags for visibility

Make sure children can properly see through masks or make-up for safe street crossing

Check costumes to make sure there aren’t obstructions that could cause trips or falls

Keep an eye on the weather forecast and dress appropriately for a more comfortable evening

Walk on sidewalks rather than in the streets, watch for vehicles and parents should assist children when crossing streets

Carry lights or flashlights for additional visibility

Anyone driving during the trick-or-treat hours must use additional caution, care and vigilance. Slow down and increase your awareness of trick-or-treaters.

attributes.description: Explore Pittsburgh's diverse park system spanning 176 parks across nearly 3,800 acres. From iconic regional parks to community and neighborhood parks offering local amenities and green spaces, each park reflects Pittsburgh's rich history and natural beauty!

text:
Our Parks

Explore Nearly 3,800 Acres Over 176 Parks

Pittsburgh's Regional Parks

Our regional parks are the signature open spaces of Pittsburgh.

These parks draw tens of thousands of visitors from throughout our City and the region. The public can attend grand civic events, play, and learn. Each park has a unique identity shaped by its cultural resources, historic landscape, natural features, and recreational amenities.

The Department of Public Works and CitiParks maintain approximately 1,920 acres of regional park land distributed across five parks.

Frick Park

Highland Park

Schenley Park

Emerald View Park

Riverview Park

Pittsburgh's Community Parks

We maintain approximately 300 acres of community park land.

Community parks draw people from more than one neighborhood because of the features or character they offer, and they are intended to serve multiple neighborhoods.

Allegheny Commons Park

W Ohio St, Pittsburgh, PA 15212, Pittsburgh, PA 15212

Allegheny Commons has anchored the North Side for over 150 years. The public commons predate the City of Pittsburgh’s annexation of Allegheny City. This treasured Victorian gem is our oldest park and recalls the grandeur of Central Park.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

Arsenal Park

276 39th St, Pittsburgh, PA 15201

Founded in 1907 on former Allegheny Arsenal grounds, Arsenal Park in Lawrenceville boasts trails, playgrounds, sports courts, and public art like the Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Fountain. Discover its rich Civil War legacy and ongoing revitalization efforts.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

August Wilson Park

1803 Cliff St, Pittsburgh, PA 15219

Formerly Cliffside Park, August Wilson Park honors Pulitzer-winning playwright August Wilson, renowned for his portrayal of African-American life in Pittsburgh's Hill District. Enjoy courts, playgrounds, walking paths, and skyline views in this vibrant community space.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

Market Square

Market Square, Pittsburgh, PA 15222

Pittsburgh’s Market Square is the heart of Downtown Pittsburgh. Located between Fifth Avenue and PPG Place, the historic Square is home to restaurants and entertainment. It is a popular gathering spot for civic events and the Downtown community. The Square is programmed in cooperation with the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

McKinley Park

475 Bausman St, Pittsburgh, PA 15210

McKinley Park is nestled between Pittsburgh’s Beltzhoover, Bon Air, and Knoxville neighborhoods. The 79-acre park boasts historic trees, basketball courts, playgrounds, a skate park, and woodland trails. It is also home to a mural called “Home Court Advantage”.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

Mellon Park

1047 Shady Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15232

Explore Mellon Park, a community gem with playgrounds, sports fields, a spray park, and a unique tennis bubble. Discover historic gardens, engage in arts programs, and enjoy events in the Walled Garden. Visit the Pittsburgh Center for the Arts and the historic Marshall Mansion for creative inspiration.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

Mellon Square

Mellon Square, Sixth Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15222

Mellon Square is a beloved urban park and one of two major “Squares” in Downtown Pittsburgh. The art deco park is built above a parking garage, and features a distinctive tree-lined black-and-white geometric pavement, fountains, raised flower beds and a cascading waterfall.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

Sheraden Park

1000 Adon St, Pittsburgh, PA 15204

Sheraden Park offers walking and running trails, a pool, playgrounds, sports fields, and courts nestled in West Pittsburgh. Enjoy its historic trees, woodland trail, and nearby McGonigle Park. Join us in shaping the park's future through the Sheraden Park Master Plan.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

South Side Park

2000 Julia St, Pittsburgh, PA 15210

South Side Park is unique in its location and topography — a hidden 57.5-acre community park, with traditional recreational amenities as well as natural areas that dominate its landscape. Located within the South Side Slopes neighborhood, it is bordered by the South Side Flats and Arlington neighborhoods.

Tagged as:
,
Community Parks

West End Overlook

Marlow St, Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh, PA 15205

West End Overlook offers breathtaking views of Pittsburgh from its perch above the Ohio River. This four-acre park features walking paths, a playground, sports fields, and public art. Enjoy the renovated space with modern amenities, perfect for gatherings and events.

Pittsburgh's Neighborhood Parks

Neighborhood parks are the basic building blocks within the Pittsburgh's parks system.

These locally-oriented parks provide residents with nearby access to the outdoors and recreation. Neighborhood parks typically include features such as picnic areas, playgrounds, open lawn, courts, and walking paths. Find your neighborhood park in the below table.

Pittsburgh's Riverfront Parks

River access is highly valued in Pittsburgh. We maintain approximately 51 acres of riverfront parks. Many partner organizations such as the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and the Sports & Exhibition Authority also maintain signature public riverfront properties.

Our riverfronts also feature a significant public trail system along the Allegheny, Monongahela, and Ohio riverfronts.

Allegheny Landing Park

Allegheny Landing, Pittsburgh, PA 15212

Nestled between the Roberto Clemente and Andy Warhol Bridges on the North Side, Allegheny Landing Park was Pittsburgh’s first modern riverfront park.

Tagged as:
,
Riverfront Parks

North Shore Riverfront Park

North Shore Riverfront Park, Pittsburgh, PA 15212

Discover North Shore Riverfront Park, a scenic gem with biking and walking trails, riverfront access, public art, and breathtaking views of the Downtown skyline. Enjoy the historic Water Steps, Fred Rogers Tribute, and various memorials in this vibrant green space.

Tagged as:
,
Riverfront Parks

Point State Park – Pittsburgh’s Confluence

Point State Park, 601 Commonwealth Pl, Pittsburgh, PA 15222

Point State Park sits at the confluence of Pittsburgh’s Three Rivers. The triangular plot of land at the tip of "The Golden Triangle" is a significant place Pittsburgh’s story and the birthplace of our community. It is a gathering place for Pittsburgh’s residents, the County, and the Commonwealth for grand civic events, and is a point of pride in our region.

Tagged as:
,
Riverfront Parks

South Shore Riverfront Park

South Shore Riverfront Park and Trail, Pittsburgh, PA 15203

South Shore Riverfront Park, just feet from the South Side Works, showcases the beauty of Pittsburgh’s Monongahela River. It contains parts of the Three Rivers Heritage trail, which runs along all three rivers throughout the entirety of Allegheny county, displaying information about historical events and river ecology along the way.

Three Rivers Heritage Trail

Three Rivers Heritage Trail, Pittsburgh, PA 15203

The Three Rivers Heritage Trail is Pittsburg's signature trail system. The 33 mile system is maintained by the Department of Public Works in cooperation with the Friends of the Riverfront.

text:
Community Festival Program Grant

Enjoy the diverse heritage, food, and entertainment of Pittsburgh's neighborhoods. Throughout the year, community festivals celebrate city living and showcase the best features of our thriving neighborhoods.

About the Grant

In existence since 1977, the Community Festival Program Grant has provided funding to help communities introduce and maintain neighborhood-focused festivals for over 40 years. The program's goal is to provide financial assistance to community groups so they may launch and develop an annual event to celebrate their community and foster togetherness. Grantees are selected by committee and based on specific criteria. All approved grant applications receive up to $1,000.00 in reimbursed funds to assist with the operations of their festival.

The festival season is from June 1 to October 31.

Who is eligible to receive a CFP grant?

To be eligible for funding, your organization and event must meet
all
of the following criteria:

Applicant must be a non-profit, tax-exempt, Pittsburgh community-based organization;

The organization must have been in existence for at least three years;

The festival must take place in a City of Pittsburgh neighborhood, be free and open to the public (festival cannot charge admission or otherwise condition entry to the event), and to the benefit of the community at large;

The festival may take place over more than one day, however, in alignment with program goals, priority will be focused on one-day events.

For full program details, please
read the 2026 Community Festival informational document here
(PDF, 256KB)
or e-mail
cfpgrant@pittsburghpa.gov
.  Note that this document is updated each year - be sure to read the complete packet.

The 2026 Community Festival Program Grant application window is now closed. Applicants should receive a response regarding their award status on or around Friday, May 29.

Let's Sort It Out - Hard To Recycle Spotlight

Electronic Waste (TVs, Microwaves, Printers, Computers)

Noble Environmental

City of Pittsburgh residents can make appointments to recycle their electronics through our vendor, Noble Environmental, starting in 2026. Options include weekly drop offs, community events, and curbside pickups. Fees apply based on material type and quantity or weight.

Residents can start signing up for drop-off and community events on Noble’s website
.

Check back here for more information on curbside collection coming soon!

Evolution E-Cycling –
Visit Evolution E-Cycling website for more information

Residents can drop off many electronics for free at their Southside location or 1 of 12 Guardian storage sites. TVs, CRTs, and printers are only accepted at the Southside location and carry a fee.

Pennsylvania Resources Council

PRC will host County-wide events in 2026.
Visit PRC's website for more information
! PRC events will no longer be hosted at 3001 Railroad Street.

Batteries (All Types, Single-Use or Rechargeable)

When batteries are disposed curbside, they can cause fires inside trucks. City of Pittsburgh residents can recycle
all
batteries through our vendor, Noble Environmental, starting in 2026. See the e-waste section for more information.

Staples

Staples will give you points when you recycle household batteries, technology, and more!
Go on Staples website for more details
, and when you go to the store, head to checkout to redeem your points with a team member!

Frick Park Environmental Center

You can drop off household disposable, single-use alkaline batteries inside the Frick Park Environmental Center free of charge.

Construction Junction

Only accepts standard alkaline batteries for 25 cents a battery. No rechargeable batteries, tools, or electronics accepted. Terminals of each battery
must
be taped over because even the residual energy of a spent battery can start a fire. Any kind of tape will do. Construction Junction also accepts electronic ballasts and magnetic ballasts for $1 per pound, rounded up in half pound increments.

Freon Appliances (Air Conditioners, Refrigerators, Dehumidifiers)

Freon-containing appliances have different disposal requirements based on size. City of Pittsburgh residents can recycle small freon appliances, (AC units, dehumidifiers), through our vendor, Noble Environmental, starting in 2026. See the e-waste section for more details.

Duquesne Light Company

Read about Duquesne Light’s Watt Choices program
will pay you $50 to recycle that old, energy-wasting refrigerator, freezer, or AC unit and $35 per dehumidifier. They may also haul it away for free! Check terms and conditions.

Appliance Warehouse

Recycle large freon appliances (refrigerators and air conditioners) at Appliance Warehouse (20 S 6th St, Pittsburgh, PA 15203). There is no charge to drop off.

Construction Junction

There is a $10 handling fee for small refrigerant-containing appliances and a $20 handling fee for big refrigerant-containing appliances (working or non-functioning, donating or recycling). When you bring any refrigerant appliance here for donation or recycling, you must come into the store to pay the fee at the front register
first
so the staff can evaluate your item.

Located at 214 North Lexington Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15208. Give them a call at (412) 243-5025 for more information.

HHW (Paint, Cleaner, Oil, Solvent, Chemicals, Anti-Freeze)

Noble Environmental

City of Pittsburgh residents can make appointments to safely manage household chemicals through our vendor, Noble Environmental, starting in early 2026. Options will include weekly drop offs, community events, and curbside pickups. Fees apply based on material type and quantity or weight.

Residents can start signing up for drop-off and community events on Noble’s website
.

Check back here for more information on curbside collection coming soon!

Pennsylvania Resources Council

PRC will host County-wide events in 2026.
Visit PRC's website for more information
! PRC events will no longer be hosted at 3001 Railroad Street.

Scrap Metal (Brass, Copper, Tin, Aluminum, Steel)

Residents can drop off scrap metal for recycling in the red metal dumpsters located at the Public Works 2nd, 3rd, and 5th Division. Accepted items include solid metal objects, pots, pans, wire, doorknobs, as well as metal gutters, fencing, siding, shelving and/or storage cabinets.
Visit our website for information
on addresses and hours. The City
does not offer
payment for scrap metal.

Local dealers may offer payment for scrap metal, including Michael Brothers, AAA Scrap Iron & Metal, Keystone Iron & Metal Co., Northside Scrap Metals, and Summit Recycling of Penn Hills. Call ahead to confirm accepted materials and current rates.

Auto Recycling (Auto Parts, Whole Vehicles, Lead Acid Batteries, Tires)

Whole Vehicles and Auto Parts

Whole vehicles can be recycled at D&D Auto Salvage, All Foreign Auto Parts, U-Pull-&-Pay Pittsburgh. You must bring the title and may receive payment for the vehicle.

D&D Auto Salvage and many scrap metal dealers, such as the ones listed previously, accept auto parts. Call businesses in advance to confirm accepted materials.

Lead Acid Batteries

City of Pittsburgh residents can recycle lead acid batteries through our vendor, Noble Environmental, starting in 2026. See the e-waste section for more information.

AAA Scrap Iron & Metal, Keystone Iron & Metal Co., Northside Scrap Metals, and Summit Recycling of Penn Hills are some scrap metal dealers that may pay cash for lead acid batteries. Call in advance to confirm.

Advance Auto Parts, Auto Zone, O’Reilly, and other auto parts stores may pay customers a $10 in-store credit for a lead acid battery. Call in advance to confirm.

Tires

City of Pittsburgh residents can use Public Works 2nd, 3rd, and 5th Divisions to drop off tires for recycling. Two (2) tires, rims removed, are allowed per day, per resident. Visit our website for
hours and locations
.

This resource is not exhaustive and does not represent endorsements.
Email recycling@pittsburghpa.gov
if you offer a recycling service and want added to the list.

text:
Plan and Track Your Trip

Know Before You Go

No matter where you're heading, PRT offers several tools to help you get where you're going when you need to be there.

Every PRT vehicle is equipped with a GPS tracker that can be tracked in real-time via
TrueTime
. The site also has an easy-to-use trip planner and other useful information.

All of our vehicles accept cash and we offer a variety of
fares and passes
to make getting to your destination seamless.

When you arrive at your stop and a vehicle is approaching, make sure you check the illuminated head sign above the vehicle's windshield for the route number. If you're not sure it's the correct one, ask the operator before you board.

Once you're on your vehicle, have a seat and watch for your stop. Our vehicles are equipped with visual displays that will tell you the next stop name.

When the vehicle is approaching your stop or station, pull the yellow cord along the window to let the operator know you'd like them to exit.

Plan Your Trip

To get started, visit
TrueTime

and select "Trip Planner" to plan a trip.

Select your starting and ending locations and you'll receive step-by-step directions, including when and where to catch your bus, rail car, or incline. |

Track Your Ride

Find out when your bus or train is coming with a real-time arrival countdown. |

More Ways to Track Your Ride

Station Signage | Many of our bus and light-rail stations have electronic signs showing real-time arrival information.
By Phone | Call 412-442-2000 and follow the voice prompts for next bus information. It helps to have your Stop ID ready.
By Text | Text your Stop ID Number to 41411 . You’ll instantly receive a text back showing the next arrivals for that stop.

text:
Leadership Team

Meet Our Leadership Team

Katharine Kelleman, CEO

Katharine Kelleman has the pleasure to serve as chief executive officer of Pittsburgh Regional Transit, the public transit system serving the Pittsburgh region.

She is responsible for the daily operations of a 700-vehicle bus fleet and an 80-vehicle light-rail system that provide service to more than 130,000 riders a day. She also oversees the organization's capital and operating budgets; partners and builds relationships with regional stakeholders; and develops and manages local and federally-funded projects that enhance and expand transit access.

Since taking the reigns as CEO in 2018, Katharine has focused on providing safe, reliable, and more affordable and accessible transit service to the Pittsburgh region. She has established better communication with riders, fought to find creative solutions for a more equitable fare system, and championed the development of a 25-year plan for the agency.

Before coming to Pittsburgh, Katharine served as CEO at Hillsborough Area Regional Transit (HART) in Tampa, Fla. and previously held leadership roles in Baltimore and Dallas. She began her career as a transit planner in San Angelo, Texas.

Katharine received her Bachelor's degree in history from the University of Colorado and her Master's degree in public administration from San Angelo State University.

She is a member of the American Institute of Certified Planners and serves on the Board of Directors of the American Public Transportation Association, United Way of Southwestern Pennsylvania, Queens Gambit, WTS International, and PWN, the Professional Women's Network.

Katharine lives in Mt. Lebanon with her husband and two sons.

text:
Projects and Programs

From new stations to better accessibility and faster service, PRT projects are designed to improve how people move throughout our region.

Bus Line Refresh

PRT's Bus Line Refresh proposes changes to the bus network to better fit the needs and new travel patterns of riders across Allegheny County.

Learn More About the Proposed Changes to Your Bus Route

Programs

Climate Action Plan

The climate action plan represents the set of actions PRT will take across the agency over the next two decades to meet our goal of zero emissions by 2045.

Learn More

Corridor Planning

Investing in existing and building new transit corridors.

Learn More about Corridor Planning

Energy & Resilience Plan

PRT aims to diversify its energy usage to reduce costs and increase efficiency

Learn More About PRT's Energy & Resiliency Plan

Landscape Design Guidelines

These guidelines are used by PRT to design and maintain its properties throughout Allegheny County.

Read more about PRT's Landscape Design Guidelines

Light Rail Accessibility

Ensuring ADA accessibility and improving access to light rail stations.

Learn More about Light Rail Accessibility

Public Art

Integrating art into PRT's system to inspire pride, curiosity, and connection.

Learn More about PRT's Public Art

Station Improvements

Investing in existing and new busway and light rail stations.

Read More About Our Station Improvement Program

Transit-Oriented Development

Advancing equitable and sustainable development around transit.

Learn More about our Transit-Oriented Development Program

Active Projects

PRTX University Line Bus Rapid Transit

PRT is building dedicated infrastructure to improve transit service in Downtown Pittsburgh, Uptown, and Oakland with its first "PRTX" on-street bus rapid transit project.

Read more about the PRTX University Line Bus Rapid Transit Project

Panhandle Bridge Rehabilitation

The Panhandle Bridge carries PRT's light rail vehicles across the Monongahela River. This $58 million rehabilitation project is expected to take approximately 32 months.

Learn more about the $58 million Panhandle Bridge Rehabilitation project

Rail Optimization Study

Pittsburgh Regional Transit (PRT) is evaluating the light rail system and developing a strategy for its future.

Read more about the Rail System Optimization Study

Belasco Station Improvements

PRT is working to improve the conditions and design of Belasco Station on the Red Line in Beechview.

Read more about the Belasco Station Improvements Project.

Bethel Village Station

PRT and local partners will be redesigning the station to improve accessibility by making the facility more comfortable, sustainable, attractive, and easier to use.

Learn More about the Bethel Village Station project

Bus Stops and Project Coordination

The bus stop is the first point of contact between the passenger and the bus service. The spacing, location, design, and operation of bus stops significantly influence transit system performance and customer satisfaction. However, since most bus stops are located on municipal or state right-of-way, not PRT-owned properties, we must work closely with our partners at municipalities and PennDOT to ensure bus stops meet our guidelines.

Read more about bus stops and project coordination

Carnegie Park & Ride Expansion Project

This project plans for modernization and enhancements of Carnegie Station along the West Busway

Read more about the Carnegie Station Project

Dormont Junction Station Improvement Project

This project would redesign Dormont Junction Station to provide opportunities for future development, increase transit use, and improve station access.

Learn more about the Dormont Junction Station Improvement Project

Hamnett Station

Creating a better, more connected station on the MLK Jr. East Busway and transit-oriented development on PRT property.

Read more about plans to improve Hamnett Station

Herron Station Area Plan

Plans are in the works to improve Herron Station, located along the Martin Luther King Jr. East Busway at the intersection of Polish Hill, Lower Lawrenceville, and the Strip District.

Learn more about the Herron Station Area Plan

Homestead to McKeesport Transit Access Improvements

This project will make it easier and safer for people to get to bus stops, add amenities to bus stops that improve the overall experience, and improve transit speed and reliability between Homestead and McKeesport and primarily along State Route 837.

Read more about Homestead to McKeesport Transit Access Improvements

Rail Grinding

PRT began its three-year rail grinding project in 2025. The third and final phase of the project is expected to begin in January 2027.

Learn more about the rail grinding project

St. Anne Station

PRT and local partners will be redesigning the station to improve accessibility by making the facility more comfortable, sustainable, attractive, and easier to use.

Learn more about St. Anne Station

Station Square Station Redesign

This project involves redesigning the Station Square Station for both light-rail and bus service serving the site. This area is critical to PRT's transit system and links three light rail lines, the Monongahela Incline, and multiple on-street bus routes.

Read more about the Station Square Station Redesign Project

South Hills Junction

Making the station safer and more welcoming, increasing station access, and encouraging future transit-oriented development.

Learn more about the South Hills Junction Station Area Plan

Wilkinsburg and Brushton Stations

PRT is seeking to create a new Wilkinsburg Station closer to businesses and the heart of the community, easier to use and navigate, and provide an open space that can be filled with art and programming by the community. PRT has also proposed creating a new station in Homewood between North Braddock and Brushton Avenues that will be within walking distance to most of Homewood community.

Read more about Wilkinsburg and Brushton Stations

Coming Soon

East/Central River-to-River Connection

This project will study opportunities to establish a new transit corridor that would connect Pittsburgh’s Strip District, Hill District, Oakland, and Hazelwood neighborhoods.

Learn more about the East/Central River-to-River Connection

East Busway Extension

This project will develop a plan for extending the MLK Jr. East Busway from its current endpoint at Swissvale Station eastward through Rankin, Braddock, and East Pittsburgh.

Read more about the East Busway Extension

Completed Projects

Downtown Escalator Project

PRT replaced nine escalators at three Downtown light rail stations in 2024.

Learn more about the Downtown escalator project

High Platform Station Improvement Project

Pittsburgh Regional Transit rehabilitated 18 high platform light rail stations between February 2022 and December 2024.

Learn more about the High Platform Station Improvement Project

Monongahela Incline Rehabilitation Project

PRT made several upgrades to the nation's oldest continuously-operating funicular during this project, which was completed in 2024.

Learn more about the 2023-2024 Monongahela Incline Rehabilitation project

Mt. Lebanon Tunnel Ventilation Project

Pittsburgh Regional Transit replaced the emergency ventilation system of the Mt. Lebanon Transit Tunnel between January 2022 and September 2024.

Learn more about the Mt. Lebanon Tunnel Ventilation Project

Mt. Washington Transit Tunnel Track Replacement project

Pittsburgh Regional Transit closed the Mt. Washington Transit Tunnel from February through December 2025 to replace more than 1,000 feet of light-rail track and conduct additional work.

Learn more about the Mt. Washington Transit Tunnel Track Replacement project

Negley Station Improvement Project

The Negley Station Improvement Project transformed the East Busway station with improved access, new passenger amenities, enhanced safety features, and landscaping. It was completed in June 2023.

Learn more about the Negley Station Improvement project

NEXTransit Downtown

The NEXTransit Downtown Plan was completed in the summer of 2023 and recommended new routes for PRT bus services in Downtown Pittsburgh that are more efficient and improve amenities for riders and complement the PRTX University Line Bus Rapid Transit project.

Learn more about NEXTransit Downtown

Plinth Project

Pittsburgh Regional Transit successfully completed the multi-year Downtown subway concrete plinth project in February 2025.

Learn more about the plinth project.

PRT Board

The Board's Role

Pittsburgh Regional Transit is governed by an 11-member Board of volunteers appointed by state and local elected officials. Four members are appointed by the Allegheny County executive; two members are appointed by the Allegheny County executive with County Council approval; and one member each is appointed by: the governor of Pennsylvania; the President Pro Tempore of the Senate; the Senate Minority Leader; the Speaker of the House of Representatives; the Minority Leader of the House of Representatives.

The Board establishes policies and provides strategic oversight for the agency, and makes key decisions by adopting operating and capital budgets and engaging with stakeholders.

text:
August 2026 Ridership

PITTSBURGH
–
Pittsburgh Regional Transit saw continued ridership growth in August 2026, as the agency recorded a 5.3% year over year weekday ridership increase.

PRT provided 3,409,352 unlinked passenger trips in August 2026. System ridership also increased 8.7% on weekdays compared to the prior month.

Weekdays

Average weekday ridership for August 2026 was 129,614 unlinked passenger trips across all modes. Weekday bus ridership was 116,222, an 8.7% increase from July 2026 and a 4.4% increase from August 2025. Weekday rail ridership was 12,740 which is a 10.6% increase from July 2026 and 15.9% higher than August 2025.

Saturdays

Average Saturday ridership was 81,343 unlinked passenger trips across all modes, which is 8.1% more than the previous month and 0.5% more than August 2025. Saturday bus ridership was 71,932, a roughly 4.2% increase compared to August 2025 and 11.7% more than July 2026. Rail ridership was 8,053, an 18.5% decrease compared to August 2025 and a 12.9% decrease from July 2026.

Sundays

Average Sunday ridership for August 2026 was 56,143 unlinked passenger trips across all modes. Bus ridership was 50,852, a 3.9% increase compared to July 2026 and slightly less than August 2025 at 2%. Rail ridership was 4,655, a 9.8% decrease compared to August 2025.

text:
Two Rail Closures Planned for This Weekend

PITTSBURGH
– Two closures will affect rail service this weekend, Pittsburgh Regional Transit announced today.

The first closure will temporarily suspend light rail service between First Avenue and Steel Plaza stations from the end of service on Friday, October 23, through the start of service on Sunday, October 25.

During the closure, crews from PRT’s Way Department will replace a switch, while crews from the Power and Signals Department will replace a signal.

Shuttle buses will operate between First Avenue at First Avenue Station and on Ross Street at Steel Plaza Station. A rail shuttle will operate between Steel Plaza and Allegheny stations. All stations will remain accessible, and PRT employees will be available at Steel Plaza to assist riders with transfers.

The second work area will close the Mt. Washington Tunnel between 5 p.m. Sunday, October 25, and start of service on Monday, October 26, while Duquesne Light does electrical work within the tunnel.

During the closure, all inbound and outbound light rail service will detour through Allentown. A rail shuttle will operate between the outbound platform of Station Square and Allegheny Station to maintain service along the corridor. Bus service will also be detoured. Inbound buses will generally use Allentown streets, while outbound service will use the Wabash Tunnel.

Riders should expect delays of up to 20 minutes during both closures.

For full detour details, visit
rideprt.org/Detours
.

Riders with questions are encouraged to contact Customer Service by calling 412-442-2000, on X @PghTransitCare or via live chat at
www.ridePRT.org
.

text:
2 New Music Venues Will Soon Liven Up the Pittsburgh Scene

Your guide to making the most of the rest of summer while planning ahead for end-of-year fun.

Pittsburgh’s culture has been shining through in fun and quirky ways this summer. There were pickle-centric cocktails temporarily available at downtown hangouts (the
Spritzery pop-up
,
Space Bar
) and themed
Pirates
games like
Yinzerpalooza
, featuring giveaways like the coveted
Dr. Robby bobblehead
doled out to the first 20,000 attendees. If you’re still in the market for a bobblehead, be one of the first 21,000 fans at the game on Tuesday, September 15, to bring home a mini version of hometown hero Roberto Clemente.

Music
has filled our fields and amphitheatres all summer long, with the luckiest artists (like
Lisa Loeb and O.A.R
)
receiving perfect-10 weather on the evening they hit the stage. We’ve been especially happy to learn of sweet, unique collaborations this month like one between
the Black Keys (who played Stage AE Monday, August 3) and The Peach Truck
, which allowed fruit-loving Yinzers to pick up juicy treats for themselves ahead of time. (We discovered that band members have been friends of
The Peach Truck
for years, so the connection felt natural for everyone involved. They say this partnership celebrates something bigger than peaches or music, and is about “preserving and sharing the traditions that make the South so special.”)

LOOKING TO AN ARTS-FILLED SEASON AHEAD

Never fear, plenty of concerts are still left in the season, including those that are
free
. A few other shows topping our radar include:
Zac Brown Band:
Love & Fear Tour
August 13 at
PPG Paints Arena
with
Old Crow Medicine Show
, who in June released their new album called Union Made.
PPG
also welcomes Kacey Musgraves (September 8), Olivia Rodrigo (September 29 and 30) and
The Red Stray Clays
(October 1). Then there are happenings at
Thunderbird
, from rising singer/songwriter
Solya
(September 4) to captivating storyteller/singer/songwriter
John Craigie
(September 10). Mr. Smalls welcomes
Margaret Glaspy
(September 18) and
Nation of Language
(September 21), while
Stage AE
brings in Sierra Ferrell and Seattle folk/Americana band
The Brudi Brothers
(September 1) plus Ohio folk talents
Caamp
(September 25).
As we look ahead, the coming months will see us slowly filling calendars with indoor fun, too — from
concerts
and
lectures
to
story slams
and
comedy shows
(hello…
Golden Girls
!). And in very exciting second-half-of-2026 news, there will be several brand-new venues ready to welcome us in in the months to come.

WELCOMING CITIZENS LIVE AT THE WYLIE

By October, there will be a new, 4,000-capacity venue in town, and there’s much buzz around its opening. Tom Loudermilk, Pittsburgh Market President, Live Nation, says that
Citizens Live at The Wylie
will fill an important gap in Pittsburgh’s live music ecosystem as the only year-round, indoor venue of its size. “That flexibility will help grow the city’s music scene and attract touring artists who may not previously have had the right place to perform here,” he predicts.

The venue is being touted as an investment in the Lower Hill. Loudermilk says it’s projected to generate $66 million in annual economic impact, create around 350 permanent jobs and support neighborhood residents, businesses and cultural institutions through several long-term community commitments.

There’s been talk of a venue like this for a decade, since Pittsburgh has always had passionate music fans and a vibrant concert scene. Loudermilk believes there’s been a need for a purpose-built, indoor venue of this size. Citizens Live at The Wylie was created to fulfill that while investing in one of the city's most historic neighborhoods.

From the beginning, the vision was to create more than just another concert venue. We wanted to build a destination that attracts world-class artists, creates memorable experiences for fans and honors the rich musical heritage of the Lower Hill District.

Tom Loudermilk

Loudermilk also adds how rewarding it’s been to watch that vision take shape over the past few years.

The venue’s been called a physical homage to an iconic era of Pittsburgh hospitality and nightlife, since the Lower Hill District once played an incredible role in shaping Pittsburgh's musical identity. Some of the greatest jazz musicians in history performed here, and the neighborhood was known for its vibrant scene and sense of community.

“We want guests to feel connected to the history of the neighborhood while experiencing a modern venue that will help write Pittsburgh's next chapter in live entertainment,” Loudermilk says. That history is reflected throughout the building with artwork, historic imagery and references to iconic neighborhood landmarks. And thanks to a partnership with the Carnegie Museum of Art, works from the Charles “Teenie” Harris Archive can also be seen in the venue.

So what to expect as a first-time visitor? “From the moment fans arrive, we want every part of the experience to feel seamless and memorable,” Loudermilk says. Fans can take in a show from the general admission floor, seated balcony, premium suites or in exclusive hospitality spaces. A rooftop lounge offers views of downtown Pittsburgh, while the Vinyl Room is an intimate listening lounge inspired by Japanese high-fidelity listening bars that features a curated record collection, chef-driven fare and creative cocktails.

“Together, these spaces are designed to make a concert feel like a full night out,” Loudermilk says. “At the end of the day, we want people to remember not only the artist they saw, but the experience they had.”

He’s personally impressed by just how much thought went into honoring the neighborhood, which will be visible in nods to the Hill District's musical legacy woven throughout the spaces. Yet all the conveniences and technology expected of a modern entertainment venue will be present too. The premium hospitality spaces have been designed as “destinations,” they say, whether folks gather here pre-show or simply soak in the atmosphere throughout the evening.

A venue of this size can offer great versatility, which is reflected in the opening calendar.
On the roster
so far, you’ll find artists spanning hip-hop, rock, pop, country, R&B, metal and comedy. Think Wiz Khalifa (October 2), Foster the People (October 4), Chelsea Handler (October 9), Boyz II Men (October 16) and Smokey Robinson (October 23), and that’s only a sampling of what’s already booked.

Loudermilk can’t wait for that first moment when the lights dim and thousands of fans get to experience this venue together. “You can design a building and plan a concert,” he says, “but it's the connection between artists and audiences that brings it to life.”

He adds that that's what Citizens Live at The Wylie is all about — “creating a place where fans can feel close to the music, artists can connect with the crowd and Pittsburgh has a venue that will create unforgettable memories for decades to come.”

MAKING MUSIC MAGIC AT MIC DROP

On the North Shore, a new nightlife destination called Mic Drop will bring 4,321 square feet in which to enjoy live entertainment, music, craft cocktails and what developers have described as “elevated social experiences.” It’s set to open by the end of the year.

Herky Pollock, president and CEO of
Legacy Hospitality Partners
, says the idea for this concept has been an evolution. Above all, he and his team strongly believe the North Shore has become the preeminent entertainment district east of the Chicago. “We are seeing more and more customers craving live entertainment,” he says. “We are leaning heavily into this niche and offering different forms of live music.”

Mic Drop will be a fully immersive experience, he promises. “One day you will be a performer, and the next you will be the audience.” It will be a place to play both night and day, and to “let loose in a fun, experiential way.”

Compared to other venues around town, this one will stand out for its mix of offerings, from “bandeoke” and karaoke to dueling pianos and live performances. Everyone can get involved; various forms of participatory entertainment will happen throughout the month.

“We will have day parties so that you can party in the day and be home by 10,” Pollock says. “We will also have parties for late night. There will be something for everyone,”

So what part brings Pollock the most excitement? “Bandeoke,” he says. “You will be the star in your own band. Who wouldn’t want to do that?”

He adds that Mic Drop will be the perfect complement to recently-opened
SugarBird
, The Plaza at North Shore and the soon-to-be-opened Highball Social Club, as well as their expansion of
Shorty’s
. As a huge proponent of all things related to this city, Pollock says, “We could not possibly be more bullish on Pittsburgh and the North Shore.”

text:
Pittsburgh Fall Festivals 2026 Guide

Colorful foliage. Crisp air. Pumpkins. What's not to love about Fall?

As the temperatures start to cool down,
fall festival season
begins heating up! Explore a pumpkin patch at a scenic farm, celebrate at cultural festivals in the city and more with Pennsylvania's stunning fall colors as a backdrop. Happy Fall!

Halloween fans, we have a
list of haunts
and
ghost tours
in Pittsburgh for you, too.

October

November

September

Kickoff and Rib Festival

September 3-7, 2026
Acrisure Stadium | 100 Art Rooney Avenue, Pittsburgh

Western PA football kicks off right at
Acrisure Stadium
, home of the Pitt Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers! Enjoy five days of football, amazing ribs, live music, the area's largest cornhole tournament and more at this free fest.

ReelAbilities Film Festival

September 3-13, 2026
Various locations in Pittsburgh

The ReelAbilities Film Festival presents award-winning films through the lens of individuals living with disabilities. In addition to impactful films, the festival also features artwork and special guests to bring the themes of community and shared human experience to the forefront. ReelAbilities is a program of
Film Pittsburgh
.
Pittsburgh Soul Food Festival
September 4-6, 2026
Market Square/Boulevard of the Allies between Stanwix and Wood Streets

Enjoy a Soulful Taste of the Burgh at this free festival spotlighting Black culinary, butchery, and food businesses. While the fantastic food takes center stage, a small business market, live music, BBQ contest, and cultural activities make this event an all-day affair!

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Acrisure Stadium (@acrisurestadium)

Britsburgh
September 8-13, 2026
Various locations in Pittsburgh

Bringing a bit of Britain to Pittsburgh, the 2026 Britsburgh Festival is chock-a-block with events from afternoon teas and cask tapping to Shakespeare performances and even a polo match, all designed to bring people together over a shared love of all things British!

Pittsburgh Irish Festival

September 11-13, 2026
Carrie Blast Furnaces | 801 Carrie Furnace Boulevard, Pittsburgh

Guests at this year’s
Pittsburgh Irish Festival
can expect to see their favorite Irish international, national, and local acts in person at the event’s 34th Annual Celtic Celebration! The line-up features new bands, phenomenal
solo performers
, well-known favorites, local Irish dance groups, and more on four stages for non-stop fun and enjoyment.

The Original Pittsburgh Taco Festival

September 12, 2026
The Stacks at 3 Crossings | 2875 Railroad Street, Pittsburgh

Pittsburgh's top tacos and food trucks take over the
Strip District
! Enjoy this
community-centered event
, which features more than 25 food trucks and vendors, plus live music, an art market, and
family fun
. This festival is produced with the support of the Pittsburgh Hispanic Development Corporation and Latin American Cultural Union.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Pittsburgh Taco Fest (@pghtacofest)

Pittsburgh Soul Food Festival

September 4-6, 2026
Market Square/Boulevard of the Allies between Stanwix and Wood Streets

Enjoy a Soulful Taste of the Burgh at this free festival spotlighting Black culinary, butchery, and food businesses. While the fantastic food takes center stage, a small business market, live music, BBQ contest, and cultural activities make this event an all-day affair!

Phantom Fall Fest

Select Dates: September 12 - November 1, 2026
Kennywood | 4800 Kennywood Boulevard, West Mifflin

Experience Kennywood's new Phantom Fall Fest! Visit the park during the day for family-friendly fun, including festive food and a unique Kennywood autumn atmosphere. After dark, the Phantom takes screams to the extreme with seven haunted houses and four scare zones.

Screenshot: Asian Film Festival

September 16 - September 23, 2026
Harris Theater and the University of Pittsburgh | 809 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh

Harris Theater is hosting an Asian Film Festival, showcasing 12 feature films and 10 short films that highlight Asian culture and experience. Ranging from animated shorts to television episodes to modern movies, the event offers a variety of media fit for whatever you're looking to enjoy.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Screenshot: Asia (@screenshotasia)

Pittsburgh International Jazz Festival
September 17 - 20, 2026
The August Wilson African American Cultural Center | 980 Liberty Avenue

Head to the August Wilson African American Cultural Center for our annual International Jazz Festival. This event brings classical jazz as well as modern jazz to the main stages of Pittsburgh and curates an impressive lineup of musicians ready to showcase their musical talent.

15th Annual Ukrainian Food Festival
September 18-19, 2026
St. Peter & St. Paul Ukrainian Orthodox Church | 220 Mansfield Boulevard, Carnegie

The Parish of Sts. Peter & Paul Ukrainian Orthodox Church will host their annual Ukrainian Food Festival in September this year. Shop traditional Ukrainian baked goods, grab plates of classic dishes, and enter your name to win one of the event's raffle baskets.
Panda Fest
September 18 - 20, 2026
Station Square East Lot Parking | 73 East Carson Street, Pittsburgh

Celebrate Asian culture with 80+ Asian food vendors and over 200 street vendors at the Panda Fest right here in Pittsburgh. Try dishes from China, Japan, Korea, Thailand, Vietnam, and more, then shop local artisans' goods, from art to clothing to accessories and more.

After shopping, sit in on one of the cultural programs, featuring traditional art, dancing, performances, and more live entertainment. Centering this event is the festival's mascot, pandas! Snap a picture with the many panda posters, inflatables, and themed treats.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Panda Fest Pittsburgh (@pandafestpittsburgh)

Penn Brewery Oktoberfest
September 18-20 & 25-27, 2026
Penn Brewery | 800 Vinial Street, Pittsburgh

Pittsburgh's classic Oktoberfest is back at Penn Brewery for 2025! Join us the weekends of September 19-21 and 26-28 at Penn's Northside location for fresh beer, German food, and live oompah music!

Pittsburgh Chinese Cultural Festival
September 19, 2026
Mellon Park | 1047 Shady Avenue, Pittsburgh

Come experience the biggest Chinese community event in Pittsburgh at this free festival. Celebrate Chinese heritage, watch traditional performances, listen to beautiful music and enjoy some delicious food.
Jump Cut Pittsburgh Noir Film Festival
September 19, 2026
The Parkway Theater & Film Lounge | 644 Broadway Ave, Mckees Rocks

Be part of the inaugural Jump Cut Noir Film Festival! 2026 marks the first-ever Noir Film Festival in Pittsburgh, which is scheduled to feature indie films, filmmakers, cocktails, Q&As, workshops, and mingles for those who adore the niche film genre.
FestPGH
September 19, 2026
Highmark Stadium | 510 W Station Square Drive, Pittsburgh

On Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, Highmark Stadium will resound with the music of bands including the headliner Switchfoot, as well as laughter, games, family fun, service opportunities and worship during the inaugural FestPGH music and arts festival.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by PGHchineseculturalcenter (@pghchineseculturalcenter)

South Park Hay Day

September 19 & 26, 2026

19th: Hartwood Acres Park | 4000 Middle Road, Allison Park
26th: South Park Fairgrounds | 1888 Brownsville Road, South Park Township

Join Allegheny County Parks for a day full of free, family-friendly fall activities. Families can enjoy hay rides, a hay maze, a pumpkin patch trip, a barnyard petting zoo, and more. Food, beverages, and snacks will be available for sale from food trucks and vendors.

Sharpsburg Summer Jam Music Festival & Bicentennial Drone Show

September 19, 2026
Kennedy Park | 1311 N Canal Street, Sharpsburg

Close out the summer with a live performance at the Sharpsburg Summer Jam Music Festival & Bicentennial Drone Show. The event will bring together incredible local performers, taking to the stage throughout the day from 1 pm to 6 pm. Dance to the music and eat from their lineup of food trucks, enjoy family-friendly activities, and drink brews from Sharpsburg's own brewmasters.

Evans City PumpkinFest
September 19 & 20, 2026
Evans City | East Main Street, Evans City

Evans City is ringing in the new season with its fifth annual PumpkinFest. Featuring live music, fall festivities, food trucks, wagon rides, car shows, free games, and more, the festival will take over East Main Street with community fun for all.
Fall Migration Festival
September 20, 2026
Stormy Oaks Nature Conservancy | 120 Forsythe Road, Valencia

Celebrate over two decades of local wildlife education and rehabilitation at Wildbird Recovery’s 15th Annual Fall Migration Festival, an annual fundraiser where supporters of all ages spend time outdoors, enjoy delicious food, and learn about different aspects of our local wildlife.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Wildbird Recovery (@wildbirdrecovery)

Four Chord Music Festival

September 25 - 26, 2026
F.N.B. Stadium | 510 W Station Square Drive, Pittsburgh

The 2026 lineup at the Four Chord Music Festival is sure to rock, with bands like Knocked Loose, Pierce the Veil, Mayday Parade, and Boys Like Girls. If you're into rock music or just love the music scene, reserve your tickets and get ready for a weekend-long festival of concerts, fun, and local community.

Reserve your tickets for the event on the
Four Chords' website
.

73 Hour Record-Breaking Infinite Cypher - Hip Hop Festival
September 25 - 28, 2026
Forest Farms | 441 Grange Hall Road, Tionesta

Feel like breaking a world record? Bring your friends and dance it out at the 73 Hour Infinite Cypher Hip Hop Festival. Looking to break the Guinness World Record for the longest rap marathon event, the Hip Hop Festival will be running for 73 straight hours (that's over 3-days long!).

This is a camping event, so be sure to pack your backpack and have your camping equipment ready to get the most out of the festival.
Butler Fall Festival
September 26, 2026
Downtown Butler, PA | Main Street

The Butler Fall Festival takes place on Main Street in Butler, PA. The event will include a car show, kids activities, artisan and craft vendors, food vendors and music!
Tropical Forest Panama Festival
September 26, 2026
Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens| One Schenley Park, Pittsburgh

Celebrating its Tropical Forest Panama exhibit, the Phipps Conservatory is throwing a festival that will have educational programs and cultural celebrations. Learn more about Panamanian culture, try Latin American food from Pittsburgh's own El Sabor Latin Kitchen, and explore Phipps' latest garden.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by INFINITE ♾️ CYPHER (@infinitecypher)

The Pittsburgh Great Race

September 26- 27, 2026
Starts at Frick Park at Beechwood Boulevar

Lace up your running shoes and challenge yourself to the annual Great Race right here in Pittsburgh. Compete in the 5K, 10K, or the junior race for any families with track stars in their midst. For every registration, the race donates $1 to the Richard S. Caliguiri Amyloidosis Fund, which supports medical research conducted here in Pittsburgh.

Pittsburgh Silent Film Festival

September 27 - October 4, 2026
Various location in Pittsburgh

Enjoy twelve films from the silent film era screened at eight venues throughout Pittsburgh, all with live musical accompaniment.

October

Oktoberfest Pittsburgh
October 1-11, 2026
Downtown Pittsburgh

Taking place over 11 days, this year’s event will be held at Fort Duquesne Boulevard, utilizing the westbound roadway from Stanwix Street to 7th Street and incorporating the 6th Street Bridge. This year promises an even better celebration of culture, food, music, and community, so festivalgoers can fully immerse themselves in German-inspired activities for all ages!
Confluence PumpkinFest
October 2-4, 2026
Confluence | Along Routes 281 and 523

Participate in a Fall Foliage celebration during the Confluence PumpkinFest. The festival includes a variety of events like the Pumpkinfest Queen Pageant, a 5K run/walk, an antique and classic auto show, a parade and a largest pumpkin contest.
Reel Q Film Festival
October 2 - 10, 2026
Multiple Locations

The 41st annual Reel Q Film Festival has announced its 2026 dates. A staple of the Pittsburgh film scene, this festival highlights queer filmmakers and stories with their multi-day festival that takes over Carnegie Mellon University in October. See new film premieres, catch local short films, and even get the chance to meet young filmmakers with tickets to the Reel Q festival.

Purchase tickets on the
Reel Q official website
.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Downtown Pittsburgh (@downtownpitt)

Jack O’Lantern Extravaganza

October 2 - November 1, 2026
Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium | 7370 Baker Street, Pittsburgh

Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium
will illuminate the city with thousands of artistically carved pumpkins glowing on your night walk through this gourd-geous new display. ZooBoo trick-or-treating will also return during daytime hours, the last two weekends of October.

Leechburg Annual Fall Festival

October 3, 2026
Leechburg Riverfront Park | Kiski Avenue, Leechburg

Head to Leechburg for fall-themed activities, games, local makers, crafters, vendors, fall-inspired food and treats, music, and family-friendly Halloween festivities. The annual fall festival is free for you to attend and brings a day of festival fun to the riverfront park, which offers a great view of the water as a backdrop to the event.

Mars Applefest
October 3, 2026
145 Grand Avenue, Mars

Experience the Mars Applefest with food, fun, shopping, games, crafts, 150+ vendors and entertainment.
Festival of Combustion
October 3, 2026
Carrie Blast Furnace | 801 Carrie Furnace Boulevard, Pittsburgh

This one is sure to be lit fam (is that what the kids say?). The hottest fall festival returns to Carrie Blast Furnaces with hands-on demonstrations, tours of the property, live music, craft beer, and food trucks.
Fall Apple Fest
October 3, 2026
Portersville Steam Show Grounds | 1512 Perry Highway, Portersville

A vintage village, sawmill, cider press, Amish donuts, antique car rally, gas engines, oilfield equipment, farm animals, train rides, steam engines, flea market, crafts, food, kids’ pedal tractor pulling, tractor pulls, and a steam building are some of the features to enjoy.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Rivers of Steel (@riversofsteel)

Pumpkin Festival

Weekends in October starting October 3, 2026
Reeger's Farm | 755 Laurel Road, Shelocta

Start a new family tradition at Reeger's Farm! On Saturdays and Sundays in October, they offer hayrides, a pumpkin patch, food trucks, and more.

Freedom Farms Fall Fest

Weekends in October starting October 3, 2026
Freedom Farms | 434 Overbrook Road, Valencia

Any weekend in October, enjoy tons of fall activities like tractor rides, a corn maze, a hay mountain, a petting zoo, pick-your-own flowers, pumpkin carving and decorating, and lots more family-friendly activities.

Autumnfest
October 3-18, 2026
Seven Springs Mountain Resort | 777 Water Wheel Drive, Champion

Treat yourself to a spectacular weekend in the mountains and enjoy the best of Pennsylvania's
beautiful fall foliage
! Hop on the chairlift for an aerial view of the fiery colors of autumn. Shop from local artisans and crafters, enjoy live music, and take a mini getaway in the mountains during Autumnfest.
Autumn Serenade Luncheon Cruise
October 7, 14, 10 & 17, 2026
Gateway Clipper Fleet at Station Square | 350 West Station Square Drive, Pittsburgh

Enjoy a tasty autumn harvest lunch while taking in the sights of Pittsburgh's fall foliage on a riverboat tour.
Fort Ligonier Days
October 9-11, 2026
Fort Ligonier | Various locations

Fort Ligonier Days is a three-day festival that commemorates the Battle of Fort Ligonier, a key engagement of the French & Indian War. The festival features historic battle reenactments, live music, authentic crafts, delicious food and more.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Seven Springs Mountain Resort (@7springspa)

Houston Pumpkin Festival

October 9-11, 2026
124 West Pike Street | Houston, PA

Features family fun for all ages, including over 175 food and craft vendors, music and entertainment, children's games and activities, a parade, and many pumpkin-related contests. Free admission.

Annual Country Fall Festival

October 9-11, 2026
Downtown Zelienople | Various locations

Enjoy two days of musical entertainment, three towers of paranormal ghost walks, pumpkin and costume contests, chainsaw carving, petting zoo, free horse-drawn wagon rides, and historic encampments and demonstrations during the Zelienople Country Fall Festival.

And while you're there, check out the Sleepy Hollow Festival in Historic Harmony! You can even take advantage of a shuttle that runs between the two towns to enjoy everything both festivals have to offer!

Pittsburgh Dragon Boat Festival

October 10, 2026
Pittsburgh Brewing Company | 150 Ferry Street

Head down to the Allegheny River to cheer on riverboat teams as they compete to win the festival's boat race. After the race, swing by some of the vendors and be sure to drop a donation or two with the festival team, as this event supports breast cancer survivors in a one-of-a-kind festival.

Fall Flower Show

Opens October 10, 2026
Phipps Conservatory & Botanical Gardens | 1 Schenley Park, Pittsburgh

With the blockbuster Summer Show, Alice in Wonderland-themed displays are here to stay through the fall! Opening Sat., Oct. 10, Fall Flower Show: Alice’s Adventures in Autumn combines the whimsy of Phipps’ unique take of Lewis Carroll’s story with our stunning chrysanthemums — and a few spooky surprises!

You'll see all your favorite characters from the book among expertly grown chrysanthemums in an endless variety of shapes, colors and sizes. Phipps has been creating chrysanthemum-themed seasonal shows since 1894, making its Fall Flower Show the longest-running in the nation and a Pittsburgh tradition that you can't experience anywhere else!

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Three Rivers Rowing Association (@3riversrowing)

Dormont Street & Music Festival

October 10, 2026
Patomac Avenue | Dormont

Join us for the Dormont Street and Music Festival, one of the community’s most anticipated events of the year. Taking place rain or shine, this free, all-ages festival offers a full day of live music across three stages featuring 18 bands, along with a wide variety of food, unique arts and crafts, and activities for all. Explore more than 60 vendors, support local businesses and artisans, and enjoy the energy and spirit of the Dormont community with family and friends.

Pittsburgh Coffee & Chocolate Festival

October 17, 2026
Monroeville Convention Center | 209 Mall Boulevard, Monroeville

The Pittsburgh Coffee & Chocolate Festival is a celebration of all things coffee and chocolate-related… and then some! Attendees will sample a variety of coffee roasts and styles, along with a multitude of decadent chocolate-themed sweets from local and surrounding-area businesses.

Pittsburgh Monster Pumpkins Festival
October 17-18, 2026
Pittsburgh Strip District

Join in on the action during the Pittsburgh Monster Pumpkins Festival, featuring a "Costume Caper" 5K run/walk, pumpkin regatta, pumpkin pie eating contest, giant pumpkin sculptures, and, of course, record-breaking giant pumpkins. This year's event is in the Strip District, at 3 Crossings Campus along 28th & 29th Street.
Fall Fest at the Pittsburgh Playhouse
October 23 - November 1, 2026
Pittsburgh Playhouse | 350 Forbes Avenue, Pittsburgh

The award-winning
Pittsburgh Playhouse
at Point Park University, a multi-disciplinary arts and entertainment center located in Downtown Pittsburgh, announces the return of Downtown Pittsburgh’s second annual multi-day Fall Fest and the family-friendly hit sensation, Boo’s Halloween House Party. Visitors of all ages can enjoy food & drinks, games, local vendors and arts & crafts onsite of the Pittsburgh Playhouse, with activities on Forbes Avenue during the weekend.

Trick or Trolley

October 24-25, 2026
Pennsylvania Trolley Museum | 1 Electric Way, Washington

Come to the Pennsylvania Trolley Museum to trick-or-treat among the antique streetcars! Visit tables run by local businesses and organizations and collect all kinds of candy and holiday favors. Costumes are encouraged for all ages!

November

Three Rivers Film Festival

November 4 - 15, 2026
Multiple Locations

Mark your November calendars for the annual Three Rivers Film Festival. If you love indie filmmaking, support the local arts, or simply love a good movie, the Three Rivers Film Festival gives you the opportunity to catch brand-new films from emerging artists. The event also hosts workshops for those looking to sharpen their craft or break into the industry.

Grab your tickets on the
Three Rivers Film Festival website
.

Latin American and Caribbean Festival

November 7, 2026
Wesley W. Posvar Hall, 1st Floor | 230 South Bouquet Street, Pittsburgh

It's official! The Latin American and Caribbean Festival has become the largest and most significant gathering of Latin American and Latinx communities in Western Pennsylvania! Don't miss out on the event's cultural celebrations, performances, foods, and more!

Yes, our fall calendar is pretty impressive, but it's just the tip of the iceberg for all the incredible events we host in Pittsburgh. Visit
our Events page
for more festivals, happenings, and offbeat events that take place year-round in the city.

text:
Carnegie Museum of Art and Natural History

Website

Email

Explore two world-class museums with one ticket at Carnegie Museums of Art and Natural History! Located in the Oakland neighborhood, the museums provide an experience filled with culture, creativity, and exploration to all who visit. Carnegie Museum of Art, renowned for its collections of more than 100,00 objects, features a range of visual art, including painting, sculpture, decorative arts, design, and photography. Located within the same historic building, Carnegie Museum of Natural History is home to one of the country’s largest and most celebrated natural history collections featuring 22 million objects and specimens, ranging from real dinosaur fossils and dazzling gems and minerals to iconic wildlife dioramas.
